body.name: Switching protocol-to-branch cover incidence
body.construction:
For \(\alpha=(j,\omega)\in\Omega\), define \(\mathsf{Succ}_{\alpha}(S,\ell,T,\tau)=1\) exactly when \(S\in\Pi\); the oracle reply for \(S\) is not \(\bot\); the event \(H_{\mathrm{slice}}(S,\ell)\) actually used to form the slice has positive mass in the returned support table; \(T\) is a measured-ancestry single-district source factor extracted from \(\operatorname{Slice}(S,\ell)\); and \(\tau\) is a valid successful \(\operatorname{IDENTIFY}^{+}\) transcript for the concrete assignment and equality type \(\omega\) of \(C_j\).  For every protocol mask set
\[
 K_{\mathrm{sw}}(S)
 =\{\alpha\in\Omega:\exists(\ell,T,\tau)\ 
       \mathsf{Succ}_{\alpha}(S,\ell,T,\tau)=1\},
 \qquad
 w(S)=\sum_{a\in S}c(a).
\]
Only legal protocols with non-\(\bot\) oracle replies can have a nonempty incidence set.
